messages.content: Can we finish Denver airfare? Hampton is held Aug. 24-26. I need enough Tuesday margin for a quick check-in or bag drop before the 6 p.m. reception, and Thursday may run to 12:45. Please compare the remaining round trips and tell me whether the United 3:35 return is the one to ticket.

Shortlist, economy/no checked bag assumed:
Option | Fare | Timing | Margins | Trade-off
United ORD nonstop | $318 | Tue 1:55-3:37, Thu 3:35-6:58 | hotel about 5:05 by rail/rideshare; Thu airport arrival about 2:00 with rideshare | cleanest, +$54
Southwest MDW nonstop | $264 | Tue 2:10-3:50, Thu 5:05-8:25 | fine margins | cheaper, but later home and MDW
Frontier ORD | $221 | Tue 3:25-5:05, Thu 6:20-9:44 | Tuesday too tight | fees/late return
I would ticket United.
For United, does the Tuesday arrival really leave time if early check-in is not ready?

Yes, with a carry-on. Land 3:37, train or rideshare gets you downtown around 4:45-5:00, then Hampton bag drop/check-in attempt. You would not have much cushion for a major delay, but it is realistic for making a 6:00 reception without a car.
And Thursday if the roundtable ends right at 12:45?

Leave the room by 12:55, collect the bag at Hampton, and use rideshare rather than rail. That should put you at DEN around 1:55-2:05, about 90 minutes before the 3:35 departure. Southwest buys more cushion but turns a reasonable workday into an 8:25 MDW arrival for only $54 saved.
Then ticket United, economy from ORD. No upgrades unless they are free; window seat if selectable, aisle is fine. Traveler is Marisol Greene, carry-on only.

Ticketed: United ORD-DEN Tuesday Aug. 24, 1:55 p.m.-3:37 p.m.; United DEN-ORD Thursday Aug. 26, 3:35 p.m.-6:58 p.m. Economy total: $318. Window requested where free; no checked bag added. Hampton stay remains unchanged with the quiet-room request and Aug. 21 cancellation deadline.

messages.content: Quick Denver timing check before I go: final email moved Thursday roundtable to another downtown building and says it may run to 1:00. Hampton confirmed bag storage but not early check-in. Keep the 3:35 United return?

Keep it, but make Thursday a rideshare plan. Tuesday: land 3:37; if storms are active, rideshare straight to Hampton, drop the rollaboard if the room is not ready, then head to the 6:00 reception. Wednesday is simple: included breakfast, in-room coffee/mini-fridge, and several quick dinner options within a few blocks.
What's my latest safe departure from the meeting?

Treat 1:00 as the hard stop. If you leave then, bag pickup at Hampton about 1:10 and rideshare by 1:15 gets you to DEN around 2:00, leaving roughly 95 minutes. Rail is okay only if you are released earlier. I would keep the flight and put a 12:55 nudge/1:00 exit on the calendar.

messages.content: I’m back from Denver and need to start Providence for Sept. 28-30. It’s a grant-site visit: community library archive, a neighborhood arts education partner, then a Thursday funder debrief. Flying from Chicago, no rental car. I may have a 5:30 p.m. host check-in Tuesday, so I need a real arrival buffer. Can you compare flying into Providence with a connection versus Boston nonstop plus train, and hotels near downtown or the train station?
Yes. What room-rate guideline should I use, and how late does the Thursday debrief run? Also, should I treat MDW as acceptable or limit this to ORD?

Target is about $235 per night before tax, and I’d like the trip under roughly $1,150 all-in if that’s realistic. Debrief should end around 1:00 Thursday. I don’t want a return that only works if we finish early. Economy only. MDW is acceptable if the value is strong; ORD is easier but not $150 easier.
Got it. I’ll price three paths: PVD via connection, Southwest-style PVD through MDW, and BOS nonstop plus rail to Providence, then match them with downtown/train-station hotels.
Please include breakfast, room coffee/fridge if listed, nearby dinner options, and cancellation terms. No booking yet.

Flight paths that fit the meeting windows:
Route | Fare plus transfer | Tuesday arrival shape | Thursday return shape | Trade-off
ORD-PVD via EWR, United | about $428 air + $50 PVD rideshares | 8:20-1:36, hotel about 2:05 | 2:35-6:08 via EWR | ORD and closest airport, but connection both ways and the 2:35 return is thin if debrief slips
MDW-PVD one-stop, Southwest | about $372 air + $50 rideshares | 9:05-2:25, hotel about 2:55 | 3:05-5:55 | good Providence timing and no Boston transfer, but MDW and open seating/check-in logistics
ORD-BOS nonstop + train | about $246-$256 air + $85-$95 rail/local transfers | 10:05-1:28, Providence about 3:40 | 5:10-6:55 from BOS | cheapest and safer Thursday cushion, but more handoffs
That Boston price is better than I expected. What are the hotel options?

Downtown/train-station hotels:
Hotel | Est. 2-night total | Access | Breakfast/room basics | Dinner/cancel notes
Hampton Inn & Suites Providence Downtown | $506 | 9-10 min walk from station; archive/debrief likely walkable or short ride | breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | restaurants on Westminster/Weybosset nearby; cancel by Sept. 26, 6 p.m.
Homewood Suites Providence Downtown | $558 | closest to station/river | breakfast included; full fridge/kitchenette and coffee | easy downtown dinners; cancel by Sept. 25
Graduate Providence | $532 | very central | no included breakfast; coffee listed, mini-fridge to confirm | on-site cafe/restaurant; cancel by Sept. 26
Courtyard Downtown | $489 | central, a bit farther from station | no free breakfast; coffee and mini-fridge listed | bistro on site; cancel by Sept. 26
Can you pair totals? Hampton looks promising; Homewood only if the logistics justify the extra.

Best pairings:
Pair | Est. total | Timing | Amenities | Main trade-off
BOS nonstop + Hampton | about $850 | Tue hotel around 3:45-4:00; Thu 1:35-ish train target for 5:10 BOS flight | breakfast, coffee, mini-fridge; good downtown dinner access | cheapest; requires Logan-South Station-Providence handoff
Southwest MDW-PVD + Hampton | about $928 | Tue hotel around 3:00; Thu 3:05 PVD return works after a 1:00 debrief | same Hampton amenities | simpler local transfer; MDW and higher fare
United ORD-PVD + Hampton | about $984 | Tue earliest hotel arrival; Thu 2:35 return is okay only if debrief ends on time | same Hampton amenities | ORD, but more expensive and connection risk
BOS nonstop + Homewood | about $902 | similar Boston timing, slightly closer to station | breakfast plus kitchenette/full fridge | +$52 for a suite; not necessary unless you want more room
On Boston, where do I lose time? I don’t want three transfers if the debrief slips.

The time loss is mostly Logan to South Station, then the train. Thursday works if you aim for an Amtrak around 1:35-1:45 or an MBTA fallback shortly after. That gets you to Boston with plenty of time for a 5:10 BOS-ORD flight. If the debrief runs past 1:30, Boston becomes less elegant but still salvageable with a later train or a costly Providence-to-Logan rideshare. The 2:35 PVD return is actually less forgiving if the meeting slips.
So the United PVD return at 2:35 is too tight if they talk until 1:15?

I would call it too tight. You would need to leave, collect your bag, get to PVD airport, and clear security with very little cushion. With carry-on only it might work on a perfect day, but it is not the option I’d build around for a funder debrief.
What about Tuesday with Boston? I need to look collected by 5:30, not arrive in a heap.

The Boston path still works Tuesday. ORD-BOS 10:05-1:28, then Logan to South Station and a Providence train puts you at the Providence station about 3:40, Hampton about 3:55. That gives roughly 90 minutes to check in or at least drop your bag before a 5:30 host check-in. A one-hour flight delay would make it tight but not impossible.
Then United via PVD seems like connection risk plus a tighter return, for more money.

That’s my read. It only wins if you strongly want ORD plus the smaller Providence airport. For this agenda, BOS nonstop plus Hampton is the best value; Southwest into PVD is the simpler-transfer backup.
Does Hampton have a queen one-bed? If it’s the same flexible rate, I’d rather hold that than anything with doubles.

Yes. I see a flexible standard queen non-smoking at the same estimated $506 total. There is also a king study at the same rate. Both list breakfast included, in-room coffee maker, and mini-fridge. The queen keeps the room type straightforward; I can add a quiet-room request.
Please hold Hampton refundable, queen if available, quiet room request. Save Boston nonstop plus train as first flight choice and Southwest PVD as backup. Do not ticket flights yet.

Held: Hampton Inn & Suites Providence Downtown, Sept. 28-30, flexible standard queen non-smoking room, quiet room requested, estimated total $506 with taxes. Cancellation deadline saved as Sept. 26 at 6 p.m. I noted included breakfast, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, and nearby downtown dinner options. No flights ticketed. Saved flight ranking: 1) ORD-BOS nonstop plus Providence train, targeting a 5:10 p.m. BOS-ORD return; 2) Southwest MDW-PVD one-stop with the 3:05 p.m. return; 3) United ORD-PVD via EWR only if avoiding the Boston transfer becomes more important.
